old_problem: The title, Procedure and Criteria name three potentially distinct firmware identity concepts—FW Version, Compliancy and Core Version. The prior review required engineering to choose one authoritative field and therefore left the case Pending. DeepSeek's generic SMBIOS/BMC strings neither observe the UI nor establish equivalence. A separate earlier row, Functionality|365|Wistron-BIOS-00032-V002, owns a direct Core Version check, while formal queue sequence 91 / row 1436 separately owns the user-approved complete BIOS flash and before/after WebUI BIOS-version coverage.
disposition_reason: No semantic equivalence or single winning label is needed. Preserve every source phrase as an independently identified checkpoint on the same BIOS Main page: capture FW/BIOS Version if that labeled property exists, capture `Compliancy`, and capture `Core Version`; compare each applicable label/value to a separate owner-approved entry in the exact platform/build manifest. A field may be absent or not applicable only when the platform BIOS UI specification says so. The operator records genuine console evidence and exits without saving; mapped SMBIOS Type 0 or BMC inventory may corroborate but cannot replace the UI. Missing expected strings or label mappings are bounded Project configuration and yield NOT READY, not Engineering Decision Pending. This row performs no flash and cannot inherit row 1436's mutation coverage.
decision_basis: Master XLSX physical rows 1432-1437, exact row-1433 DeepSeek columns, tests.json, exact GPT second review, locked selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and the related row-365 Core Version review were read directly. The true next formal queue identity is row 1436 / variant 69759b3dcd2307c2, not merely the next physical worksheet row.

Firmware release/version, vendor core codebase version and compliance level can be different values. Similar strings or placement on one page do not prove equivalence, so the Review layer does not rename, collapse or infer any mapping.

The conflict can be removed without choosing among the three source nouns: a union acceptance matrix contains one row per named concept, exact UI label, expected value and applicability authority. All applicable rows must pass independently; one matching field cannot mask another mismatch.

DMTF SMBIOS Type 0 standardizes BIOS Information fields such as BIOS Version, release date and firmware revisions, but it does not define the vendor UI labels `Compliancy` or `Core Version`. dmidecode is therefore secondary evidence only when the owner supplies an explicit mapping.

BMC FRU board information identifies hardware and is not a BIOS Main-page version oracle. BMC/Redfish firmware inventory is likewise corroboration unless the target documentation maps it to a captured UI property.

The case's core acceptance is visual BIOS setup content. A physical operator or validated KVM session must capture the actual page, label and value. OCR/API-only output, stale KVM frames or a generic dmidecode line cannot pass the case.

Navigating setup may require a controlled reboot, but the procedure is read-only: no setting is edited, no defaults are loaded, no save is performed and no firmware is flashed. The operator exits through the documented no-save path and verifies normal OS Ready recovery.
The five-minute attended and five-minute machine-time source fields are retained as planning metadata; they do not override the controlled boot/setup/return duration or create a short-cut acceptance.

ED-02/ED-21 preserve distinct row identities; ED-03/ED-04 and ED-36 make target values bounded Project configuration; ED-12/ED-20/ED-23 require genuine visual evidence; ED-17/ED-35 prevent a read-only command from replacing UI coverage; ED-37 governs read-only BIOS fields; ED-38 prohibits agent verdicts or unapproved actions.

test_case.test_name: BIOS Main-page FW Version, Compliancy and Core Version visual verification
test_case.purpose: Verify every applicable firmware-identity concept named by this source on the exact target BIOS Main page—FW/BIOS Version, Compliancy and Core Version—against separate owner-approved build-manifest entries, using genuine visual evidence and no BIOS setting change.
required_package: Exact server/board identity, BIOS image/build identifier, current BIOS version and versioned platform BIOS Main-page/UI specification

Owner-approved acceptance matrix with separate rows for source concept, exact displayed label, expected value/format and applicability authority for FW/BIOS Version, Compliancy and Core Version; documented cross-field or SMBIOS/BMC mappings only where they truly exist
Qualified operator or validated, non-stale BMC KVM/remote-console session, maintenance/reboot window, secure credentials and a documented BIOS-entry/no-save-exit/OS-recovery path
Protected evidence store, screenshot/redaction policy, target/time correlation and optional supported read-only SMBIOS Type 0 plus BMC/Redfish inventory tools
test_case.test_command: MANUAL VISUAL PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind Source Key/variant, target serial/board and approved BIOS build. Preserve baseline OS/BMC/SEL evidence without clearing it, record current read-only SMBIOS Type 0 and mapped BMC/Redfish firmware inventory only as corroboration, and confirm a safe reboot/setup window. After immediate operator authorization, enter BIOS Setup through the approved physical or validated KVM path; make no edits. Open the Main page and capture one fresh full-context image plus close evidence for every visible source-named concept: FW/BIOS Version, `Compliancy` and `Core Version`. Record exact spelling, value and page context; do not infer equivalence. Compare each applicable row independently with the approved acceptance matrix. A missing label is accepted as N/A only with cited platform UI authority; otherwise it is NOT READY/FAIL as the matrix defines. Exit without saving, return to OS Ready and verify target identity, BIOS readback, BMC health and absence of unintended setting/update activity. Do not flash; keep row 1436 and row 365 independently credited.
test_case.expected_result: The exact target and BIOS build are proven; every applicable source-named Main-page property is visibly present under the expected exact label/format and matches its own approved manifest value. Any authoritative not-applicable entry is cited. Optional SMBIOS/BMC values agree only under documented mappings. The operator exits without saving, no configuration or firmware mutation occurs, and the same system returns to OS Ready with normal BMC health and preserved evidence.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact Source Key/variant and target/build identity, a three-concept acceptance matrix, fresh actual BIOS Main-page visual evidence, independent exact comparison of every applicable FW/BIOS Version, Compliancy and Core Version entry, documented mapping for any software corroboration, no-save exit and normal OS Ready recovery. FAIL covers a wrong applicable label/value/format, authoritative manifest mismatch, UI/readback disagreement, unintended setup change or failed recovery. NOT READY covers missing build manifest, expected values, applicability authority, console/operator, maintenance window or secure evidence path. N/A is per field only and requires the target UI specification. A matching dmidecode/FRU/API value, another row's Core Version result or row 1436's flash cannot substitute.
safety_gate: A human operator owns reboot, BIOS entry/navigation and visual confirmation. Validate target identity and KVM freshness; do not use a stale or cross-target console frame.

Read-only navigation only: do not edit settings, load defaults, save, reset policy, flash firmware or accept an unexpected prompt. Exit without saving and stop on any pending-update or ambiguous state.

Preserve diagnostic evidence; never clear SEL, OS or setup logs as preparation. Protect console/OS/BMC credentials and redact only secrets, not the tested labels, values, target correlation or timestamp.
Do not guess that FW Version, Compliancy, Core Version, SMBIOS Version or BMC inventory are equivalent. Require explicit versioned mappings for comparisons across namespaces.
Do not automatically retry a missed setup-entry window, reboot or UI capture. Preserve the first outcome and obtain a new authorized run if another attempt is needed.
This record authorizes no DUT action and no hardware PASS. Firmware flash remains exclusively governed by its own case and separate safety authorization.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant, target serial/board, BIOS image/build/version, UI-spec and acceptance-matrix revisions
Fresh full-context BIOS Main-page screenshot/video with target/session/timestamp correlation and exact FW/BIOS Version, Compliancy and Core Version labels/values
Per-concept expected/observed/applicability comparison with cited authority; no inferred equivalence
Optional complete SMBIOS Type 0 and BMC/Redfish firmware inventory with explicit mapping document and tool versions
Baseline/preserved logs, operator authorization/session record, no-save exit proof, post-return BIOS readback, BMC health and OS Ready evidence
Explicit statement that no flash, setting write, default load, log deletion, retry or DUT action was performed by the review agent
test_case.recovery: If the wrong target/page/build appears, a label is ambiguous, an unexpected prompt or pending update is shown, or any setting may have changed, capture the state and stop. Exit using the documented discard/no-save path; do not guess, save, reset defaults or flash. Verify the original target, BIOS readback, BMC health and OS Ready. If normal exit or boot is unavailable, use only the pre-approved platform recovery/runbook and escalate to the BIOS/BMC owner; preserve all evidence and do not automatically retry.

source_conflict.reason: The review no longer selects or equates conflicting nouns. It preserves title, Procedure and Criteria as three independent acceptance-matrix rows on the same UI, so every source-named concept receives explicit visual coverage and its own Project oracle.

blocked.reason: The read-only UI operation and safe recovery are defined. Exact labels, expected strings and applicability are bounded platform/build configuration; their absence prevents execution but does not require a new universal engineering ruling.

external_authorities.application: Type 0 defines standard BIOS Information strings and revisions used only as mapped corroboration; it does not define vendor BIOS UI labels Compliancy or Core Version.

project_authority: The BIOS/platform owner supplies the exact build manifest, visible-label expectations, per-field applicability and any documented UI-to-SMBIOS/BMC mapping; the operations owner authorizes the controlled setup window. They cannot silently collapse the three source concepts, accept a command in place of visual UI evidence, borrow another case's result, waive no-save recovery or turn this row into the separately governed flash case.
